messages:
priya: quick share — did a small microprofile to quantify kernel-switch costs vs continuous batching across A100/H100. saw a sharp perf cliff around seqlen ~512 when we mix short+long requests. wondering if this explains the production tail spikes we saw yesterday.

maria: can you paste the raw numbers / command you ran? graphs help but raw is fine.

priya: sure — command and trimmed output below. ran 1k requests with a 70/30 mix of seq=32/seq=512, burst QPS ~120.
```
# ./perf_profile --model t5-xxl --arch a100 --mix "32:0.7,512:0.3" --requests 1000 --continuous-batching on
# summary (A100)
launch_overhead_new_kernel_us: 140
avg_token_us_cont_batch: 12.3
avg_token_us_kernel-switch: 13.6
90p_tail_latency_ms: cont_batch=210, mixed_switch=320
# toggling KV cache off: 90p_tail drops to ~240 but avg token goes up ~6%
```

jonathan: interesting. so kernel switch adds ~1.3us/token here, but the real pain is the tail from repeated launches. is the scheduler creating tiny batches that force different kernel paths too often?

eke: my hunch — KV cache behavior + sticky kernel decision interacts badly. if prefix lengths vary we can't reuse cached KV effectively and we often pick a different kernel executable (fused vs unfused) which triggers extra CUDA launches. mixing seqlens amplifies this.

maria: does H100 look different? it sometimes has different kernel layout and launch cost.

priya: ran H100 quick too. launch_overhead_new_kernel_us ~180 (slightly worse), but avg_token delta smaller. cliff still around 512 though — seems more tied to internal exec-path switch than raw launch latency.

jonathan: could we add a tiny predictor in the kernel selector: estimate amortized cost = launch_cost / expected_num_tokens_in_batch + exec_token_cost. pick path only if amortized cost lower. basically an add-on to autotuner.

eke: yes — and key is accurate expected_num_tokens. the scheduler can expose an expected-batch-token-count metric. also we should prefer grouping requests by preferred kernel id (cheap tag) in the continuous batching window. less switching.

priya: prototype pseudo:
```
// on incoming request: attach preferred_kernel_hint = pick_by(seqlen, model_shape)
// scheduler: try to assemble batches prioritizing same preferred_kernel_hint for first N ms
// selector: if launch_cost / expected_tokens > threshold => prefer existing kernel path
```

maria: that sounds reasonable. need to watch potential long-wait for tail requests if we over-group. maybe a hard timeout fallback.

jonathan: also consider KV cache bias: if we detect high KV hit-rate for a kernel path, bias towards it even if initial amortization looks marginal. KV hits reduce token compute significantly.

eke: agreed. KV hit-rate should be another input feature for the predictor. we can record a lightweight EWMA per (model, kernel_variant) during runtime.

priya: action items: 1) i'll run larger synth runs (10k mixed) on both A100/H100 and dump per-kernel EWMA + launch histograms; 2) jonathan/eke can sketch the lightweight predictor + scheduler hint API; 3) i'll open a perf ticket and attach results.

ci-bot: created RNF-294: "kernel-switch-cost-predictor + scheduler hints" (assignee: priya) :sparkles:

maria: thanks — pls include a short test that repros the cliff so we don't regress. :thumbsup:

priya: will do, I'll post the larger run results here when done.
